title: Data Lineage Tracking
summary: Track how source data becomes chunks, embeddings, prompts, model outputs, and decisions so changes and incidents can be traced to their affected artifacts.
overview: Data lineage records relationships between inputs, transformations, execution runs, and outputs. For agent systems, useful lineage extends beyond ETL tables to document versions, chunks, embeddings, retrieval sets, prompts, model configurations, tool observations, and published artifacts. Trace spans describe execution timing; lineage explains derivation and dependency.

Choose stable identifiers and appropriate granularity. A document-level link may be enough for discovery but insufficient to explain which passage supported a claim. Store references and transformation metadata rather than duplicating sensitive content in the lineage catalog. Lineage supports investigation and impact analysis; it does not prove that a transformation was correct.

production.poc: A prototype can retain source identifiers and model versions beside generated outputs. Add transformation identities before rebuilding indexes or changing chunking logic.
production.production: Production emits lineage events for ingestion and generation, preserves source versions, and links outputs to retrieval evidence and configuration. Handle deletions and revoked access across derived artifacts.
production.scale: At scale, lineage becomes a graph supporting impact queries and selective reprocessing. Avoid unbounded event cardinality by choosing meaningful artifact boundaries and retention policies.

components.name: Artifact identity
components.role: Assigns stable names and versions to sources, chunks, embeddings, and generated outputs.

components.name: Transformation recorder
components.role: Captures job, run, code, configuration, and input-output relationships.

components.name: Lineage catalog
components.role: Stores derivation edges and supports upstream and downstream impact queries.

components.name: Generation evidence link
components.role: Connects answers to retrieved passages, tool results, and model configuration.

components.name: Change propagator
components.role: Uses lineage to identify artifacts requiring invalidation, deletion, or recomputation.

flow.title: Identify source version
flow.description: Record the authoritative object, revision, ownership, and relevant access metadata.

flow.title: Record transformation
flow.description: Emit input-output relationships for parsing, chunking, embedding, and indexing runs.

flow.title: Capture retrieval set
flow.description: Associate the generation run with the actual evidence used, not every possible source.

flow.title: Link output
flow.description: Store model and prompt versions with the published artifact and claim evidence references.

flow.title: Query impact
flow.description: Traverse dependencies when a source, policy, or transformation changes.

flow.title: Apply remediation
flow.description: Rebuild or invalidate affected artifacts and record the corrective transformation history.

useCase.title: Tracing an assistant answer to an operating procedure
useCase.situation: A manufacturing support assistant answers questions about approved equipment procedures across several facilities.
useCase.problem: When a procedure revision is withdrawn, the team cannot identify which indexed chunks and generated guidance used it.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must support source-version traceability and targeted invalidation of affected content.
useCase.architecture: Ingestion records document, parser, chunk, and embedding versions; generation records the retrieved evidence set and output artifact.
runtime: An operator asks about cleaning setup, and the answer links to the exact approved procedure revision used.
When that revision is superseded, a lineage query identifies affected index entries and retained answer artifacts for review or invalidation.
useCase.failure: If a pipeline omits lineage events, its outputs remain quarantined from the controlled corpus until provenance is repaired.
useCase.impact: Measure lineage completeness, impact-query coverage, stale-artifact removal time, and reproducibility of sampled answers. Traceability does not replace procedure approval.

tradeoffs.benefit: Precise impact analysis reduces unnecessary reprocessing.
tradeoffs.cost: Metadata volume and identifier management increase.

tradeoffs.benefit: Independent pipelines can publish derivation facts.
tradeoffs.cost: Missing or delayed events can leave temporary gaps.
Investigations depend on continued access to referenced artifacts.

failures.scenario: A reindex changes chunk identifiers without mapping
failures.detection: Downstream answers lose resolvable evidence references.
failures.recovery: Preserve versioned mappings or retain the referenced chunk artifacts.

failures.scenario: Deletion removes a source but leaves derived content
failures.recovery: Propagate approved deletion or invalidation through the lineage graph.

mistakes.fix: Record durable input-output relationships and source versions.

mistakes.mistake: Linking answers to the whole corpus
mistakes.fix: Capture the actual retrieved and used evidence set.
Include chunking, embedding, prompt, and model versions.

whenToUse: Sources and transformations change over time.
Incidents require tracing affected generated artifacts.
Deletion and reprocessing need precise dependency information.
whenNotToUse: Outputs are disposable and have no retained dependencies.
Identifiers cannot remain stable across transformations.
The catalog would collect sensitive payloads without a clear purpose.
checklist: Define artifact identity and version rules.
Link answers to actual evidence sets.
